messages.subject: Re: Renjin & icCube
messages.body_plain:
Great,
You won't need devSVG or most of the graphics "devices" for R, Renjin's (incomplete) implementation writes to the standard Graphics2D API, so you can use any jvm-based graphics library that supports this API, for example batik (http://xmlgraphics.apache.org/batik/) for SVG, the standard java renderers for PNG, JPEG, etc, or the GraphicsIO library in the FreeHep project (http://java.freehep.or <http://java.freehep.org/>

But again, Renjin's base graphics implementation is incomplete, so it will take a bit of work to get say, ggplot2 working on Renjin. Take a look at the awtIntegrationTest() :

http://code.google.com/p/renjin/source/browse/trunk/core/src/test/java/org/renjin/primitives/graphics/GraphicsTest.java#79

for a starting point

Alex

On Mon, Jun 11, 2012 at 5:10 PM, David Alvarez-Debrot <dau vid.alvar...@crazy-development.com> wrote:
> Alex,
>
> The idea is to send the SVG result to a web page (we only need the svg text) to embedd into html. Using this devSVG <http://svitsrv25.epfl.ch/R-doc/library/RSvgDevice/html/RSvgDevice.html> library is possible with renjin ?
>
> Regards,
> David

messages.body_plain:
It looks like the platform string was hardcoded in renjin:
http://code.google.com/p/renjin/source/browse/trunk/core/src/main/java/org/renjin/primitives/System.java#64

I will try to get Renjin to figure out a sensible version string to provide, but we will probably need a backdoor to allow loading arbitrary packages, maybe a -Drenjin.platform=xxx property.

Will let you know when it's committed.

Alex
